reasons: The two answers are word-for-word the same except for the first link. Both open by correcting the agent's premise. Both say that a weather cancellation where the person does not take the rebooking still entitles them to a cash refund, and that accepting a credit ends that right. Both then fall short of the key in the same ways. They treat declining as 'your call' and draft the message accepting the credit, which is the deduction the key names. They ask for only 12 months and say United's credits usually last about a year, when the law requires 5 years. They give no refund deadlines (7 business days, 20 calendar days) and no refund-request message. B is slightly better because its '14 CFR part 260' link points to the regulation text on Cornell LII. A's link with the same label goes to a DOT press release, which is a small mislabel.
